finding.claim: Missing authorization on tenant wipe: wipe() calls requireRole(), which only returns a boolean and never throws, and discards the result. Any caller can wipe any tenant regardless of role. The sibling export() correctly uses checkRole(), which throws.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (any User with any or no roles) calling POST /tenants/{t}/wipe with an arbitrary tenant string
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant), which is destructive deletion of tenant data

trace.note: requireRole's javadoc says it returns true if the user holds the role and does not throw
requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role) with no exception
wipe() ignores the boolean returned by requireRole(u, "OWNER")
By contrast, export() uses checkRole, which throws SecurityException at line 20

finding.guards_checked: Only one file exists, so I looked for any other check. None exists: no caller-side or framework-level guard and no tenant-membership check. The roles are also global rather than per-tenant, so even a legitimate OWNER of one tenant could pass checkRole for another tenant in export(). That is a secondary concern, and I could not confirm it without seeing how the roles are populated.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole (Admin.java:14) returns a boolean and never throws; its result is discarded at line 26. checkRole (line 18) throws but is only used in export(). No other guard exists in the codebase.
verdict.reason: Admin.java:26 calls requireRole as a bare statement, ignoring the boolean it returns (defined at :14-15), so repo.wipe(tenant) at :27 runs for any user, unlike export() at :32, which uses the throwing checkRole.
